summary: Feed s177_triple is degraded: 3 faults detected - 99.4% encrypted traffic exceeds NDR 90% tolerance, 13.38 Gbps microbursts overload 10 Gbps tool port (134% capacity), and 28.1% ERSPAN-tunneled traffic obscures inner flows.

findings.root_cause: Near-total encryption (99.39% of bytes) - traffic is forwarded as TLS/encrypted without decryption or cleartext feed. NDR tolerates ~90% encrypted but this feed is almost entirely opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection and cannot inspect encrypted payloads; with 99%+ encrypted, behavioral and signature detection is blind, drastically reducing detection coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: NDR needs cleartext payload per profile (needs_full_payload=true); decrypting at broker/proxy or forwarding decrypted copy restores inspection capability without exceeding 90% encrypted threshold.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is sending microbursts of 13.38 Gbps in 1ms intervals to a single 10 Gbps NDR port - 134% of line rate over 2 intervals. Aggregate rate exceeds tool port capacity, likely due to no load balancing or rate limiting.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR port is oversubscribed; bursts will cause buffer drops at NIC/broker egress, leading to missed packets, broken flows, and missed detections despite packet_drops check still healthy at capture point.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute 13+ Gbps across 2x10G NDR members or add load-balancing group to keep per-port utilization below 80% threshold and prevent burst drops.

findings.root_cause: 28.1% of frames (2214/7876) arrive encapsulated in ERSPAN from packet broker/SPAN source. Broker is forwarding tunneled traffic without stripping outer header.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR must parse inner headers to correlate flows; if not configured for ERSPAN, it sees only tunnel endpoints, misses inner IP/ports and application detection, and wastes cycles on outer encapsulation.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker presents native inner frames to NDR, restoring full L2-L7 visibility and reducing overhead while preserving tunnel metadata if needed.
